To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CYP2D genotype predicts tamoxifen metabolite levels in black African breast cancer patients.
we have identified a large inter-individual variation in plasma concentration of tamoxifen active metabolite endoxifen among Ethiopian women with breast cancer.

we report the first pharmacogenetic study on tamoxifen metabolism in black African women and that CYP2D genotype and ABCB1 genotype together explain 65% of the variability of the major tamoxifen metabolite, endofixin, in plasma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel pharmacokinetic and genetic profile of tamoxifene in Ethiopian breast cancer women.
the pharmacokinetic variability of tamoxifen metabolites in Ethiopian breast cancer women.
the development of new drugs to treat cancer and to improve the quality of life of patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CYP2D genotype is the major predictor of plasma endoifen concentration.
CYP2D is the main determinant of endoxifen plasma level in this population.
CYP2D*10 is the major predictor of endoxifen level and MRE/MDM in Ethiopian breast cancer patient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CYP2D genotype is the major predictor of endoxifen level and MRE/ NDM in this population.
, CYP2D haplotype is an important predictor of plasma endogenous endoxifen level, which is a key determinant of tamoxifen efficacy.
the CYP2D genotype is a good predictor for tamoxifen treatment outcome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CYP2D is the major contributor to the inter-individual variability in tamoxifen metabolism in Ethiopians.
the CYP2D haplotype, ABCB1, CYP2D activity, and CYP2D gene dosage are important predictors of tamoxifen metabolism in black Africans.
the IIV of endoxifen concentration is high and the effect of CYP2C polymorphism on the pharmacokinetics of tamoxifen is negligible in the Ethiopian population.
